10A.7 Microsoft Entra ID Protection — Risk Detection

ID Protection scores identity risk in real time using ML-based detections (atypical travel · password spray · token replay · unfamiliar sign-in properties · leaked credentials). APEX-M consumes the signals at three layers:

  • Risk-based Conditional Access — high-risk sign-in or user blocks access; medium-risk requires step-up MFA.
  • Workload identity risk — per Securing workload identities, ID Protection flags anomalous service-principal sign-ins and suspicious credential changes. APEX-M routes workload-identity-risk events to Microsoft Sentinel where they correlate with LEDGER anomaly rows.
  • Agent identity risk — same signal set extended to Foundry agent identities; APEX-M Sentinel detection rule fires on any non-clean agent risk score and pages the on-call engineer.

10A.7.1 Agent-Specific Risk Events

Microsoft Entra ID Protection now emits a dedicated set of risk events scoped to agent identities. APEX-M wires each one to a Sentinel detection rule and a Defender for Identity action:

Risk event (riskEventType)What it meansAPEX-M response
unfamiliarResourceAccessAgent identity accessed a resource it has never accessed beforeSentinel rule emits incident; if the resource is Tier-3/4 sensitive, agent identity is auto-paused via Conditional Access until on-call review
signInSpikeAnomalous sign-in volume from the agent identity (vs its 30-day baseline)Sentinel rule emits incident; rate-limit middleware ramps down agent throughput pending investigation
failedAccessAttemptAgent identity tried to access a resource it lacks permission forIf isolated, log to LEDGER as a permission-mismatch signal; if repeated, page on-call (likely indicates a misconfigured RBAC grant or a compromised blueprint)
riskyUserSignInThe user on whose behalf the agent is operating is itself risky (OBO / delegated scenarios)Block the OBO token exchange at the middleware layer; surface to operator's session manager
threatIntelligenceAccountThe agent identity matches a known-bad indicator from Microsoft Threat IntelligenceAuto-disable the agent identity; freeze the blueprint; engagement-lead-paged incident

The events flow into the unified audit log, the new DSPM-for-AI Agents tab (§10A.14), Sentinel's AIAgentsInfo table, and Defender alerts. APEX-M's value-add over the platform: per-Service mapping from event to runtime response, so a threatIntelligenceAccount match on an HLS-E2E-04 agent triggers the strict-pause path while the same event on an RC-E2E-04 agent triggers the moderate-pause path — per Service Trust envelope (§30.1.5).

The new DSPM-for-AI surface (per §10A.14) correlates these events with agent-level prompt and tool-call telemetry, so the SOC sees a single agent-shaped record rather than reconstructing from per-event logs. Deployment Guide §5A.7 wires the event collection and §6B wires the Sentinel correlation.

10A.8 Microsoft Entra ID Governance — Lifecycle & Access Reviews

ID Governance handles the lifecycle: joiner / mover / leaver workflows, access packages, access reviews. APEX-M usage:

  • Access reviews — quarterly reviews of every PIM-eligible role assignment · agent identity inventory · workload identity inventory · per-Service group memberships.
  • Lifecycle workflows — when a Service architect joins, a workflow assigns Foundry Agent Administrator (PIM eligible), apex-shared workspace Member role, and Microsoft Teams adaptive-card test channel access. When they leave, the same workflow revokes.
  • Access packages — operator self-serve onboarding to a Service: requesting access to apex-rc-e2e-03-merch-directors triggers an approval workflow that grants the group + a Microsoft Fabric Power BI viewer role assignment.

10A.9 Microsoft Purview — The Two Halves

Microsoft Purview is the merger of Azure Information Protection (AIP) + Microsoft Compliance + Azure Data Catalog Gen 2. Two distinct halves serve APEX-M:

HalfSurfacesAPEX-M role
Data GovernanceData Map · Unified Catalog · Data Estate Insights · Data PolicyCatalog the entire APEX-M data estate (Bronze · Silver · Gold across all Services + cross-cloud SOR shortcuts) · drive lineage from SOR to operator's Power BI report · classify data for Trust-envelope routing
Data SecuritySensitivity labels · DLP · Insider Risk Management · Communications Compliance · eDiscovery · Audit · DSPM for AIEnforce what cannot leave the tenant · monitor anomalous insider behaviour · capture every Copilot prompt/response in audit log · score AI-app risk via DSPM for AI

10A.10 Purview Data Map — Catalog · Lineage · Classification

The Data Map is the foundation. Per Data Map docs:

  • Collections & Domains — collection hierarchy maps to APEX practices and Services; Data Map domains align with Microsoft Fabric domains (per Services Guide §1A.11).
  • Scans — connector-based scans of Microsoft Fabric OneLake (must be explicitly registered — not automatic), Azure SQL, Azure Cosmos DB, Snowflake, Databricks, S3, GCS, on-premises sources via the self-hosted integration runtime. APEX-M ships deployment-scripts/purview-scan-bootstrap.ps1 per Service.
  • Classifications — applied automatically during scan via sensitive info type (SIT) patterns (system + custom). APEX-M's custom SIT library covers the four-tier PII classification (Tier 1 public · Tier 2 internal · Tier 3 PHI · Tier 4 financial) plus per-practice patterns (RC SKU · HLS NPI · ER asset tag · etc.).
  • Lineage — captured automatically when supported sources transform data (Microsoft Fabric pipelines · Azure Data Factory · Databricks · Synapse). APEX-M agent calls emit lineage hints into the LEDGER which a per-tenant ETL ingests into Purview Data Map nightly so Gold-mart lineage walks back to Bronze SOR rows even when the agent transformation isn't natively understood by Purview.

Crucial APEX-M integration point: Microsoft Fabric OneLake is not auto-cataloged. Per Register and scan Microsoft Fabric, the Fabric tenant must be explicitly registered as a Purview source. APEX-M's tenant-onboarding Bicep includes this registration as a hard requirement for STAGE+ promotions.

10A.11 Sensitivity Labels — Information Protection

Sensitivity labels travel with the data — applied in Microsoft 365 (Office documents · email · Teams chat · SharePoint), in Microsoft Fabric (Lakehouse and Warehouse items), in Microsoft Purview (Data Map asset classifications). Once labelled, the label persists across systems · enforces encryption · restricts who can extract.

APEX-M label library (recommended baseline; tune per engagement):

LabelEncryptionAPEX-M usage
PublicNoneOperator-shareable summaries · public-facing KPI tiles
General — InternalNone (rights labels only)Internal operational Power BI reports · routine LEDGER digests
Confidential — EngagementEncrypt: any signed-in user in the engagement Microsoft 365 groupService-architect documents · Bicep parameter sets · MCP tool catalog manifests
Confidential — Client PHIEncrypt: explicit user list (clinical reviewers + pii-unlock service principals only)HLS Tier-3 PHI in Bronze · Direct-Lake-served clinical Power BI reports for HLS-E2E-04
Highly Confidential — FinancialEncrypt: explicit user list + co-ownerTier-4 financial data; cross-Service composition gated by dual-control unlock

Per Purview for Microsoft Agent 365, when a sensitivity label is configured for encryption, the label must explicitly grant the agent instance VIEW + EXTRACT rights — broad rights like "all users in the organization" or "any authenticated user" are insufficient for an agent identity. APEX-M's labels enumerate agent identities explicitly.

10A.12 Microsoft Purview DLP — Data Loss Prevention

DLP enforces what cannot leave: prevent sensitive content from being shared in email · pasted into third-party chat or AI · downloaded to non-managed devices. APEX-M's required DLP policies:

  • Endpoint DLP — Windows endpoints onboarded to Purview. Block paste of credit-card numbers, NPIs, and Tier-3 PHI patterns into third-party AI sites accessed via browser (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Gemini). Operator can override with justification (logged) for Tier-1/2; hard-block for Tier-3/4.
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot location — DLP scoped to Copilot can restrict prompts that contain sensitive info types or files with specified sensitivity labels (per DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot). APEX-M PROD restricts Copilot from processing Tier-3/4 content unless the prompt-context Service is the right Service (e.g., HLS-E2E-04 Copilot can process PHI; RC-E2E-03 Copilot cannot).
  • Microsoft Teams DLP — Block sensitive content in Teams adaptive cards · channel chats. APEX-M HITL adaptive cards never include raw Tier-3 PHI; the card surfaces tokens and unlock-on-approval (Trust envelope realisation, §30.1.5).
  • Exchange DLP — Block emails containing Tier-3/4 patterns from leaving the tenant.

10A.13 Insider Risk Management — Behavioural Anomaly Detection

Insider Risk Management uses ML over Microsoft 365 + indicator signals to score risky user behaviour — exfiltration, IP theft, security violations. Per policy docs, APEX-M's required policies:

  • Data leak — Tier-3/4 priority content. Flagged when a user with PHI/financial access uploads to non-managed cloud storage, prints unusual volumes, or pastes large content into non-tenant browsers. Cumulative-exfiltration detection compares behaviour to peer groups (same job title, similar SharePoint-site access).
  • Departing-user policy. Auto-activated when HR signals a user's last-day notice — increased monitoring for 30 days; cross-applies to APEX engagement teams rolling off accounts.
  • Risky AI usage policy. When users paste sensitive content into third-party AI sites or use AI-app prompts containing classified data, score is boosted. Combined with Endpoint DLP, this is the AI-specific behavioural signal.

10A.14 DSPM for AI — Data Security Posture Management for AI

DSPM for AI is Purview's AI-specific surface — it captures every AI-app prompt and response, classifies the content, surfaces sensitivity labels in answers, shows which Microsoft 365 files Copilot referenced, and gives admins one pane to manage AI-specific risk. Microsoft now ships two DSPM-for-AI surfaces — the new DSPM for AI experience (default for new tenants, agent-aware) and the original classic DSPM for AI (still available for tenants that have not been migrated). APEX-M targets the new experience: the difference matters because the new surface is the only one that inventories agents and pairs cleanly with Microsoft Entra ID Protection's agent risk events (per §14C.6). APEX-M binds DSPM for AI three ways:

  • Activity Explorer (AI activities tab) — every Microsoft 365 Copilot · Microsoft Copilot Studio · Microsoft Foundry · Microsoft Security Copilot · Copilot in Fabric · Microsoft Agent 365 · Microsoft Facilitator interaction is captured. The new experience adds a dedicated Agents tab that inventories every Foundry hosted agent, Copilot Studio agent, and third-party MCP-connected agent and surfaces a per-agent risk score. APEX-M's audit overlay reads these activities and correlates with LEDGER rows.
  • Sensitivity-label inheritance — newly created content from Microsoft 365 Copilot inherits the highest-priority sensitivity label of source files; APEX-M extends this rule to agent-generated content via ApexClassificationGuard middleware (Services Guide §14B.5).
  • Endpoint DLP for AI — block paste into third-party AI per §10A.12 above.
  • Agent risk correlation with Entra ID Protection. The new DSPM-for-AI surface pairs with Entra ID Protection's agent risk events (unfamiliarResourceAccess · signInSpike · failedAccessAttempt · riskyUserSignIn · threatIntelligenceAccount) so the SOC has a per-agent rather than per-user view. APEX-M's Sentinel + Defender wiring (§14C.7) subscribes to both feeds.

Per the Microsoft 365 Copilot Purview integration docs, prompts and responses flow into the unified audit log including the Microsoft 365 service in which the activity took place and references to files accessed. Sensitivity labels on referenced files are captured. APEX-M's compliance posture inherits this for free — no additional integration required at the Copilot layer.

Note — classic DSPM for AI is still around

Microsoft is rolling tenants from classic DSPM for AI onto the new experience in waves. Engagements landing in tenants still on classic should treat the Layer 0 readiness check as "request migration via the client's Microsoft FastTrack contact" — most APEX-M controls work on classic, but the agent-inventory and agent-risk-correlation items above do not. Deployment Guide §5A.12 has the operational checklist for both modes.

10A.15 The APEX Trust Envelope · Realised by Entra + Purview

Services Guide §30.1.5 names the Trust envelope as one of the six per-Service envelopes. Entra and Purview are how it is realised:

Trust propertyEntra ID realisationPurview realisation
Identity is verified · scoped · revocableConditional Access · PIM · ID Governance access reviews—
Behaviour is observed · scored · escalatedID Protection (sign-in & user risk · workload identity risk · agent identity risk)Insider Risk Management · Communications Compliance
Data is classified · labelled · protected—Data Map classifications · sensitivity labels · DLP
Lineage from Bronze to operator decision is preserved—Purview lineage · LEDGER hash-chain (APEX framework adds the agent-step lineage Purview cannot natively walk)
AI interactions are auditable—DSPM for AI · Activity Explorer
Cross-tenant boundaries are boundCross-Tenant Access Settings (default deny) · external collaboration policies—
Forensic anchor for "what happened"Sign-in logs · audit logs · risk reportsAudit (unified audit log) · eDiscovery · APEX LEDGER (anchored to Microsoft.KeyVault HSM CMK · WORM blob)

Per Services Guide §30.1.5: "the Trust envelope is realised, not declared." The realisation is the Entra + Purview surface laid out above. None of these primitives are APEX framework code — they are Microsoft platform services configured by APEX-M Bicep (per Deployment Guide §5A) and consumed via standard SDKs.

Independence — Entra and Purview live in the client tenant

Per the two-contract Independence model, Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Purview are client services — the client provisions and operates them; Deloitte's Microsoft practice configures them via APEX-M Bicep + deployment scripts as part of the Service-delivery engagement. No Deloitte tenant is in the trust path. ECIF or other Microsoft funding flows directly client ↔ Microsoft. The APEX framework documents the configuration; the configuration runs in the client's Entra and Purview.

Key Takeaways

  • APEX-M has five identity types — User · Group · Workload Identity · Managed Identity · Microsoft Entra Agent ID (new). Every audit trail starts with which one is invoking.
  • Microsoft Entra Agent ID is the new platform: per-published-agent identity · blueprint as governance template · Conditional Access · ID Protection · access reviews — agents are first-class governance subjects.
  • Conditional Access can target users, groups, agent identities (preview), and workload identities (Workload ID Premium licensed). Risk-based and location-based controls baseline every PROD deployment.
  • PIM elevates roles JIT with approval; ID Protection scores risky identities including workload + agent; ID Governance handles lifecycle workflows and access reviews.
  • Purview has two halves: Data Governance (Data Map · catalog · classification · lineage) and Data Security (sensitivity labels · DLP · Insider Risk · DSPM for AI). APEX-M binds both.
  • Microsoft Fabric OneLake is not auto-cataloged in Purview — Fabric tenants must be explicitly registered as Purview sources. APEX-M's tenant-onboarding Bicep enforces this.
  • DSPM for AI captures Copilot prompt/response audit, classifies AI interaction content, propagates sensitivity labels, and gates third-party AI paste via Endpoint DLP.
  • The Trust envelope (§30.1.5) is realised by these primitives — Entra grants identity, Purview classifies what flows through it, DLP enforces what cannot leave, LEDGER preserves the forensic anchor.

Catalog Drills

  1. For your engagement's primary Service, list every Entra ID identity that participates in one HITL approval flow — which user, which workload, which managed, which agent identities. Tag each with its CA policies.
  2. Inventory your engagement's PIM-eligible roles. Identify which lack dual-control approval. Justify or remediate.
  3. Run a Purview Data Map scan against the apex-rc-e2e-03-prod workspace. Inspect the lineage walk back to a Bronze SOR row. Identify the gap APEX-M's LEDGER lineage hint must fill.
  4. Audit your sensitivity label library. For Tier-3 PHI labels, verify the agent-instance VIEW+EXTRACT rights are explicitly enumerated (not "all signed-in users").
  5. Open DSPM for AI Activity Explorer for one week. Count AI interactions per Service · per persona · per sensitivity label. Compare to LEDGER rows for the same period — the gap is the cross-system reconciliation work.
Part IV

Gold Tier — Decision-Ready Data

Think back to Marisol on Tuesday afternoon. Her phone buzzed; she opened the Microsoft Teams card; she saw nine pieces of information arranged exactly so she could make the call — the SKU and lot, the affected stores, the per-store velocity, the cost-of-goods, the proposed markdown percentage, the projected margin hit, the comparable historical decisions, the expiry deadline, and the recommendation. She did not see the underlying D365 row count. She did not see the IoT calibration history. She saw the nine things that mattered for her decision, and only those. Forty-eight seconds in, she approved.

That card-shaped answer is what Gold is. Bronze preserves what the source system actually sent. Silver translates that into one consistent business vocabulary. Gold packages — already joined, already filtered, already aggregated — the specific answer-shape one specific decision needs. Each Service maintains one Gold mart per question its agents ask, and exactly one. The same Parquet bytes that feed The Pricer's MCP read also feed the merchandising director's Power BI dashboard, because both are asking the same fundamental question of the data.

The three chapters in this part build Gold from the inside. Chapter 11 covers the four canonical mart shapes (point-in-time · decision-panel · time-series · attribution) and why Gold is materialised rather than computed on-demand. Chapter 12 walks the per-Service Gold mart inventory — what shape each Service's questions take, named one by one, so you can plan a Service's Gold layer in an afternoon rather than a quarter. Chapter 13 covers the MCP tool surface — the typed contract between an agent and a Gold mart that means the agent never writes SQL of its own. Three chapters · one job: turn Silver's consistent vocabulary into the answers operators can act on.

Chapter 11

Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse Patterns

What This Chapter Does for You
  • Walks the Microsoft Fabric Warehouse + Direct Lake + semantic-model pattern for serving Gold to agents and operators.
  • Establishes the four mart shapes used across the catalog (point-in-time, panel, time-series, attribution).
  • Explains why Gold marts are materialized rather than computed on demand.
60-second read
  • Gold lives in Microsoft Fabric Warehouse (T-SQL surface) backed by OneLake Delta; Direct Lake provides zero-copy Power BI on top.
  • Four mart shapes — point-in-time · decision-panel (~40% of marts) · time-series · attribution — cover every agent question across the catalog.
  • Marts are materialized, not on-demand: latency · predictability · cost all favor materialization at APEX volume.
  • Three triggers: scheduled (cron) · upstream-event (Eventstream from Silver) · Direct Lake auto-refresh.

11.1 Where Gold Lives

Gold marts are served from Microsoft Fabric Warehouse (T-SQL surface over the same OneLake storage that hosts the Lakehouse). Direct Lake mode in Power BI lets the same Gold mart power operator dashboards without copying data into a tabular model. Semantic models on top of Gold marts are the surface analysts and HITL approvers see; MCP tools are the surface agents see. Both surfaces query the same materialized marts.

Microsoft Fabric componentResource typeRole in Gold
Microsoft Fabric WarehouseMicrosoft.Fabric/warehousesT-SQL surface · per-Service mart catalog · MCP query target
Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse (Gold zone)Microsoft.Fabric/lakehousesUnderlying Delta Parquet · OneLake storage
Microsoft Fabric Direct Lake semantic modelMicrosoft.Fabric/semanticModelsPower BI surface for operators · zero-copy over Gold
Microsoft Fabric PipelineMicrosoft.Fabric/dataPipelinesMaterialization triggers · scheduled and event-driven
Microsoft Fabric NotebookMicrosoft.Fabric/notebooksMaterialization logic · PySpark or T-SQL per mart

11.2 The Four Mart Shapes

Across the 38-Service catalog, Gold marts fall into four shape categories. The shape is dictated by the question; the question is dictated by the agent's reasoning step.

11.2.1 Point-in-time mart

"Given a key, what is the current state?" One row per key, denormalized, kept fresh by upstream Silver builds.

Examples — g_inventory_position_current (RC-E2E-05) · g_member_eligibility_current (HLS-E2E-04) · g_well_status_current (ER-OG-03) · g_equipment_health_current (ICE-EaaS-04).

11.2.2 Decision-panel mart

"Given a triggering event, what does the agent need to know to decide?" One row per triggering event with all the context joined together.

Examples — g_excursion_decision_panel (RC-E2E-03 cold-chain) · g_prior_auth_decision_panel (HLS-E2E-04) · g_outage_decision_panel (ER-PU-04) · g_irops_passenger_panel (TH-AIR-02).

This is the most common shape across the catalog — roughly 40% of Gold marts. The W2-pilot trigger pattern (event fires → decision panel materializes → agent queries it) is what produces the shape.

11.2.3 Time-series mart

"How has this metric evolved over a rolling window?" Wide rolling-window aggregations partitioned by the dimension the question asks about.

Examples — g_kpi_rc_e2e_03_daily (RC pricing KPI) · g_network_fault_trends_15m (TMT-TEL-NET-02) · g_warranty_intake_weekly (ICE-Aftermarket-03).

11.2.4 Attribution mart

"Of the outcomes observed, which came from agent-suggested actions and which came from baseline?" One row per outcome with the LEDGER decision row that drove it (or null for baseline).

Examples — g_markdown_outcome_attribution (RC-E2E-03) · g_denial_appeal_attribution (HLS-E2E-02) · g_ra_recovery_attribution (TMT-TEL-RAA-04).

Attribution marts are how the Service KPI envelope gets measured. They join LEDGER rows (decisions) with Silver outcomes (the next markdown / appeal / recovery) and produce the gross-margin lift, denial-rate drop, RA-recovery dollars that the Sellers Guide commits to.

11.3 Why Materialized, Not On-Demand

An obvious shortcut: skip materialization, let MCP tools issue ad-hoc T-SQL against Silver. It works for ten requests per minute. It breaks at the volume APEX runs at (RC-E2E-03 alone fires hundreds of agent calls per shift across a 250-store pilot, scaling to thousands at enterprise rollout).

  • Latency. Materialized Gold mart query: ~50–150 ms. Equivalent multi-Silver-table join: 2–8 seconds. The agent's reasoning step needs sub-second context.
  • Predictability. A materialized mart's row hash is stable across reads in the materialization window; an ad-hoc join's result depends on Silver freshness at query time. Audit reproducibility benefits from the former.
  • Cost. Microsoft Fabric Warehouse charges per query; one materialization burst plus N cheap mart reads is much less than N expensive ad-hoc joins.

11.4 Materialization Triggers

Three triggers materialize a Gold mart:

  1. Scheduled — Microsoft Fabric Pipeline runs on cron (most time-series and KPI marts; e.g., g_kpi_rc_e2e_03_daily runs at 02:00 each day).
  2. Upstream-event — Microsoft Fabric Eventstream fires when Silver completes a build; pipeline subscribes (most decision-panel marts; e.g., g_excursion_decision_panel rebuilds when a new excursion fires through Silver).
  3. Direct Lake auto-refresh — Microsoft Fabric Direct Lake observes underlying Delta tables and serves the latest version without an explicit pipeline (most current-state point-in-time marts; the underlying Silver table is the source of truth).

Key Takeaways

  • Gold lives in Microsoft Fabric Warehouse (T-SQL surface) backed by OneLake Delta Parquet; Microsoft Fabric Direct Lake provides zero-copy Power BI on top.
  • Four mart shapes — point-in-time, decision-panel, time-series, attribution — cover every question across the catalog.
  • Marts are materialized, not on-demand: latency, predictability, and cost all favor materialization at APEX volume.
  • Materialization triggers are scheduled (cron), upstream-event (Eventstream from Silver), or Direct Lake auto-refresh.

Per-Service Gold Marts

12.1 The Mart Inventory per Service

Every Service profile in Part VI lists its Gold marts using a uniform inventory pattern: shape · name · backs which agent question · materialization trigger · KPI contribution. The pattern is uniform; the contents are Service-specific. Architects onboarding a new Service into a tenant produce this inventory before they write any MCP tool definitions.

12.2 The RC-E2E-03 Worked Template

ShapeNameQuestion backedTriggerKPI contribution
Decision-panelg_excursion_decision_panel"For excursion X, what is the lot, the at-risk inventory, and the recent markdown history?"Eventstream rule (§5.3)Margin protected per event ($142K avg)
Decision-panelg_markdown_proposal_basis"For SKU-store S/L, what is the elasticity, competitor price, current markdown, and demand forecast?"Daily 02:00 + Silver completion eventMarkdown-to-clear ratio +41%
Point-in-timeg_inventory_position_current"For SKU-store S/L, what is on-hand right now?"Direct Lake auto-refreshDays-on-hand −28%
Time-seriesg_kpi_rc_e2e_03_daily"What is GM, DoH, markdown-to-clear by store-week?"Daily 02:00Reports the envelope
Attributiong_markdown_outcome_attribution"Of markdowns approved by HITL, which were agent-suggested vs baseline?"Daily 03:00Attributes GM lift

12.2.1 g_excursion_decision_panel — sketch

DDL — g_excursion_decision_panel
CREATE TABLE g_excursion_decision_panel (
    excursion_id        VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    store_id            VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    zone_id             VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
    fired_ts            TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL,
    -- lot context (joined from SCML.Lot)
    lot_id              VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    lot_supplier_id     VARCHAR(64),
    lot_production_date DATE,
    lot_expiration_date DATE,
    lot_fsma204_status  VARCHAR(16),
    -- at-risk inventory (joined from SCML.Inventory)
    at_risk_qty         DECIMAL(18,4),
    at_risk_value_usd   DECIMAL(18,2),
    -- markdown history (joined from MERML.Markdown)
    recent_markdowns    JSONB,        -- last 3 markdowns for this SKU
    -- excursion metrics
    duration_min        INT,
    peak_temp_c         DECIMAL(5,2),
    threshold_c         DECIMAL(5,2),
    -- materialization metadata
    silver_max_event_ts TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL,
    materialized_at     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL,
    row_hash            VARCHAR(70)  NOT NULL,    -- 'sha256:' + 64 hex
    PRIMARY KEY (excursion_id)
)
PARTITION BY RANGE (fired_ts);

One row per excursion event. All the context the agent needs in a single row. The MCP tool rc_e2e_03.get_excursion_decision_panel from §3.1 reads this mart by (store_id, excursion_id) primary key — sub-100ms.

12.2.2 g_kpi_rc_e2e_03_daily — sketch

DDL — g_kpi_rc_e2e_03_daily
CREATE TABLE g_kpi_rc_e2e_03_daily (
    store_id            VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    business_date       DATE         NOT NULL,
    -- realized margins
    gross_margin_dollars DECIMAL(18,2),
    gross_margin_pct     DECIMAL(8,4),
    -- inventory health
    days_on_hand_avg     DECIMAL(8,2),
    aged_stock_pct       DECIMAL(8,4),  -- % of inventory > 60 days on hand
    -- markdown effectiveness
    markdowns_proposed_n INT,
    markdowns_approved_n INT,
    markdown_to_clear_ratio DECIMAL(8,4),
    -- excursion outcomes
    excursions_n         INT,
    margin_protected_usd DECIMAL(18,2),
    -- baseline for attribution
    baseline_gm_pct      DECIMAL(8,4), -- 90-day pre-pilot trailing baseline
    delta_gm_pp          AS (gross_margin_pct - baseline_gm_pct) PERSISTED,
    materialized_at      TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (store_id, business_date)
);

This mart is what proves the Sellers Guide commitment. delta_gm_pp rolling up across stores produces the +3.2pp number; days_on_hand_avg rolling up produces the −28%; markdown_to_clear_ratio produces the +41%. Power BI Direct Lake on this mart drives the operator dashboard the Merchandising Director sees daily.

12.3 Naming and Partitioning Conventions

  • Mart name. g_ prefix + question shape. g_excursion_decision_panel is unambiguous; g_inventory is not.
  • Partitioning. Decision-panel marts partition on fired_ts (or equivalent triggering timestamp); time-series marts partition on the period column; point-in-time marts partition on a sensible date. Microsoft Fabric Warehouse partition prune dramatically reduces the cost of high-volume agent queries.
  • Row hash. Every materialized row carries a row_hash column that the MCP tool returns alongside the data. The agent's LEDGER row records the hash; the audit chain links back to the materialized row.
  • Materialization metadata. Every Gold table has silver_max_event_ts (newest Silver row used in the build) and materialized_at (when the build finished). These two columns are how an architect debugs "the agent decided X but the data didn't yet show Y" — the freshness window is right there.

Key Takeaways

  • Per-Service mart inventory follows a uniform pattern: shape · name · question backed · trigger · KPI contribution.
  • RC-E2E-03 has five marts spanning all four shapes; the inventory shows up identically in every Part VI Service profile.
  • row_hash, silver_max_event_ts, and materialized_at are mandatory columns on every Gold table — they make agent decisions audit-reproducible and freshness debug-able.
Chapter 13

Agent MCP Tool Surface

What This Chapter Does for You
  • Walks the MCP host implementation against Microsoft Fabric Warehouse.
  • Shows the read-tool, decision-emit-tool, and HITL-stage-tool patterns that cover every agent interaction in the catalog.
  • Establishes the per-Service tool registration manifest that propagates through Microsoft Purview and the orchestration layer.
60-second read
  • Three MCP tool patterns — read (~70%) · decision-emit (~20%) · HITL-stage (~10%) — cover every agent interaction.
  • FastAPI MCP host registers tools at startup, queries Microsoft Fabric Warehouse under mi-apex-merch-mcp, emits LEDGER rows on every call.
  • mcp-manifest.yaml per Service feeds four consumers: the host · Microsoft Purview · the orchestrator · agent prompts.

13.1 Three Tool Patterns

Every MCP tool in the catalog (~165 across all 38 Services) falls into one of three patterns. Knowing the pattern tells you the tool's audit shape, its cost profile, and its security boundary.

13.1.1 Read tool

Reads from a Gold mart. Idempotent. Free of side effects. The most common pattern — about 70% of the catalog.

  • Input: a key (or set of keys) for the Gold mart.
  • Output: the materialized row(s), with row hash.
  • LEDGER: writes a mcp.tool.called row with input args and output hash.
  • Identity: mi-apex-merch-mcp with Microsoft Fabric Warehouse Reader on the per-Service workspace.

13.1.2 Decision-emit tool

Writes a decision row to LEDGER and to a Service-specific decision table (e.g., MERML.Markdown for an approved markdown). About 20% of the catalog.

  • Input: the decision payload + supporting evidence row hashes.
  • Output: the LEDGER row ID + decision row ID + cosign attestation of the LEDGER row.
  • LEDGER: writes a decision.committed row with the full payload.
  • Identity: mi-apex-merch-mcp with Microsoft Fabric Warehouse Writer on the Service's decision tables and append on LEDGER.
  • Side effect: triggers a Microsoft Fabric Eventstream that downstream attribution marts consume.

13.1.3 HITL-stage tool

Stages a HITL approval ask, including PII unlock if needed. About 10% of the catalog.

  • Input: the proposed decision + the human approver's identity + (optional) PII unlock request.
  • Output: a stage ID the orchestrator polls; the actual decision lands when the human approves.
  • LEDGER: writes a hitl.staged row immediately and a hitl.resolved row when the approver responds.
  • Identity: mi-apex-merch-mcp + just-in-time mi-apex-merch-pii-unlock token if a PII unwrap is requested.

13.2 The MCP Host Implementation

The MCP host is a FastAPI app (Python in the MVP, with Java and .NET implementations possible). It runs as a Container App in the Service's resource group, sharing the Microsoft.App/managedEnvironments environment with the agents.

PYTHON — MCP host tool registration (sketch)
from agentic_merch.mcp import MCPHost, ReadTool, DecisionEmitTool, HITLStageTool
from agentic_merch.fabric import FabricWarehouseClient

host = MCPHost(service_code="RC-E2E-03")
warehouse = FabricWarehouseClient(workspace="rc-e2e-03")

# Read tool — backs by g_excursion_decision_panel
host.register(ReadTool(
    name="rc_e2e_03.get_excursion_decision_panel",
    gold_mart="g_excursion_decision_panel",
    input_schema=ExcursionPanelInput,
    output_schema=ExcursionPanelOutput,
    query=lambda args: warehouse.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM g_excursion_decision_panel "
        "WHERE store_id = ? AND excursion_id = ?",
        (args.store_id, args.excursion_id),
    ),
))

# Decision-emit tool — writes MERML.Markdown + LEDGER row
host.register(DecisionEmitTool(
    name="rc_e2e_03.commit_markdown_decision",
    decision_table="MERML.Markdown",
    input_schema=MarkdownDecisionInput,
    output_schema=MarkdownDecisionOutput,
    on_emit=lambda args: warehouse.transactional(
        insert_markdown=args.to_merml_row(),
        ledger_emit={"event": "decision.committed", "service_code": "RC-E2E-03",
                     "agent_id": args.agent_id, "evidence_hashes": args.evidence_hashes},
    ),
))

# HITL stage tool — stages approval, with optional pii_unlock_request
host.register(HITLStageTool(
    name="rc_e2e_03.stage_markdown_approval",
    decision_class="markdown_above_threshold",
    teams_card_template="markdown-adaptive-card.json",
    input_schema=HITLStageInput,
    output_schema=HITLStageOutput,
))

host.run(port=8080)

13.3 The Per-Service MCP Manifest

Every Service ships an mcp-manifest.yaml that enumerates its tools. The manifest is consumed by:

  • The MCP host at startup (registration source of truth).
  • Microsoft Purview (catalog registration).
  • The orchestration layer (n8n / Logic Apps Hybrid workflows reference tool names from this manifest).
  • The agent prompts (the tool descriptions in this manifest are what the LLM sees for tool selection).
YAML — mcp-manifest.yaml example (RC-E2E-03)
service_code: RC-E2E-03
service_version: 1.0.0
mcp_host: app-rc-e2e-03-mcp-lab01.azurecontainerapps.io
identity: mi-apex-merch-mcp
tools:

  - name: rc_e2e_03.get_excursion_decision_panel
    pattern: read
    gold_mart: g_excursion_decision_panel
    description: |
      Fetch the per-event decision panel for a cold-chain excursion: SKU lot,
      current inventory position, downstream risk, recent markdown history.
    consumed_by_agents: [the-analyst, the-finance-lead, the-operations-lead]

  - name: rc_e2e_03.get_markdown_proposal_basis
    pattern: read
    gold_mart: g_markdown_proposal_basis
    description: Per SKU-store, return elasticity, competitor price, current markdown, demand forecast.
    consumed_by_agents: [the-demand-checker, the-finance-lead]

  - name: rc_e2e_03.commit_markdown_decision
    pattern: decision_emit
    decision_table: MERML.Markdown
    description: Write an approved markdown to MERML and emit LEDGER.
    consumed_by_agents: [the-operations-lead]
    requires_hitl: true

  - name: rc_e2e_03.stage_markdown_approval
    pattern: hitl_stage
    description: Stage a markdown decision for HITL approval via Teams adaptive card.
    consumed_by_agents: [the-operations-lead]
    teams_target: contoso-merchandising-channel

Appendix B is the full MCP tool catalog rolling all 38 Services' manifests into one cross-reference.

13.4 How the Agent Framework Loader Wires MCP Tools onto Agents

The bridge between the mcp-manifest.yaml above and a running Microsoft Agent Framework ChatClientAgent is the APEX-M Agent Framework Loader (§14A.8). The Loader is the producer; the agent is the consumer; the manifest is the contract:

apex_m/agent_framework_loader.py · MCP-to-agent binding
from agent_framework import Agent
from agent_framework.tools import MCPStreamableHTTPTool, function_tool
from apex_m.agent_framework_loader import (
    load_agent_spec, load_use_case_workflow, resolve_tool_for_role
)

# 1. Load the agent's metadata (model · tools allowed · HITL gate)
agent_spec = load_agent_spec("apps/services/rc-e2e-03/agents/the-pricer/agent.yaml")

# 2. For each MCP tool the agent.yaml declares it can use,
#    instantiate the right Agent Framework MCP transport.
#    Transport selected by env var: laptop -> stdio · cloud -> HTTP
mcp_tools = []
for qualified_name in agent_spec.mcp_tools:
    if APEX_SUBSTRATE == "laptop":
        # Subprocess: APEX MCP host runs in docker-compose alongside agents
        tool = MCPStdioTool(
            command="apex-mcp-host", args=["--service", "rc-e2e-03"],
            tool_name=qualified_name,
        )
    else:
        # Container Apps: APEX MCP host reached over private endpoint
        tool = MCPStreamableHTTPTool(
            endpoint=APEX_MCP_HOST_URL,            # from KV-backed env var
            tool_name=qualified_name,
            header_provider=managed_identity_token_provider("apex-mcp"),
            row_hash_check=True,                   # APEX-specific extension
        )
    mcp_tools.append(tool)

# 3. Construct the agent. Same code on laptop and cloud.
agent = Agent(
    client=FoundryChatClient(),
    name=agent_spec.name,
    instructions=load_prompt(agent_spec.prompt_path),
    tools=mcp_tools,
    middleware=[
        ApexClassificationGuard(agent_spec),
        ApexPromptShieldMiddleware(content_safety_endpoint=CS_ENDPOINT),
        ApexAuditMiddleware(agent_spec),    # emits LEDGER on every invocation
        ApexHITLMiddleware(agent_spec)
            if agent_spec.hitl_gate else None,
    ],
)

13.4.1 The Row-Hash Verification Wrap

APEX-M adds row-hash verification to every MCP tool result before the model sees it. The Loader wraps each MCPStreamableHTTPTool in a verification middleware that:

  1. Receives the tool response (data + row hash from the MCP host)
  2. Compares the response's row_hash_observed against the catalog's row_hash_registry for that tool version
  3. If mismatch: raise RowHashMismatchError · emit LEDGER row · trigger Sentinel detection 3 (§32A.2)
  4. If match: the response is allowed to reach the model context window

The verification is invisible to the agent author — the Loader injects it automatically when row_hash_check=True. From the agent's perspective, the MCP tool either returns valid data or raises an exception. There is no third state where the agent reasons over un-verified data.

13.4.2 The MCP-Tool-as-Function-Tool Pattern (Inline / Single-Process Case)

Sometimes a Service's MCP tool runs inside the agent's process (laptop tier · simple Services). In that case the Loader skips the MCP transport entirely and registers the underlying function directly as an Agent Framework @function_tool:

Inline MCP-tool registration · laptop / sprint-0 prototype
from agent_framework import tool
from apex_m.mcp_catalog import rc_e2e_03

@tool
def get_excursion_decision_panel(
    excursion_event_id: str,
    sku_id: str,
    store_id: str,
) -> ExcursionDecisionPanel:
    """Fetch the per-event decision panel for a cold-chain excursion."""
    return rc_e2e_03.get_excursion_decision_panel(
        excursion_event_id, sku_id, store_id
    )

agent = Agent(client=client, instructions=..., tools=[get_excursion_decision_panel])

The inline variant is for laptop / Sprint-0 prototyping only — production agents always use MCPStreamableHTTPTool so the MCP host's row-hash registry, audit row, and Service-scoped identity all participate. The Loader picks the right path automatically based on the substrate env var; the engagement architect doesn't think about it.

13.4.3 Cross-Service Composition · MCP Tools as A2A Agents

When RC-E2E-03's Pricing Agent needs to invoke RC-E2E-09's Lot Provenance agent across Services (per §17.4), the Loader exposes RC-E2E-09 not as an MCP tool but as an A2AAgent from Agent Framework's Microsoft.Agents.AI.A2A package. The Pricing Agent's tool list gets both:

  • RC-E2E-03's MCP tools (intra-Service Gold-mart reads)
  • An A2AAgent wrapper around RC-E2E-09's published agent endpoint (cross-Service collaboration)

To the LLM, both look like ordinary callable tools; under the hood, MCP tools traverse the row-hash-anchored MCP host while A2A traverses the inter-agent protocol with Microsoft Entra agent-identity claims. The Loader handles the distinction; the agent prompt is unchanged.

Key Takeaways

  • Three MCP tool patterns — read (~70%), decision-emit (~20%), HITL-stage (~10%) — cover every agent interaction in the catalog.
  • The MCP host is a FastAPI app that registers tools at startup, queries Microsoft Fabric Warehouse under mi-apex-merch-mcp, and emits LEDGER rows on every call.
  • mcp-manifest.yaml per Service feeds the host, Microsoft Purview, the orchestrator, and agent prompts; one manifest, four consumers.
  • The Agent Framework Loader binds MCP tools onto ChatClientAgent instances; selects transport (stdio / HTTP / WebSocket) per substrate; wraps row-hash verification automatically.
  • Cross-Service composition (RC-E2E-03 → RC-E2E-09) uses A2A · the Loader exposes peer Services as A2AAgent tools alongside MCP tools; the LLM sees them uniformly.
Part V

Orchestrations

Return to Marisol's Tuesday afternoon for a moment. The Teams card that landed on her phone didn't write itself. Something fired when the IoT sensors first reported temperatures climbing — and from that single event, a sequence had to play out: an analyst agent had to score the severity, a pricer agent had to propose markdowns, a demand checker had to score per-store impact, a finance agent had to verify the proposal didn't blow the day's margin envelope, an operations-lead agent had to compose the human-friendly card, the card had to find Marisol on Teams, her answer had to commit to the canonical decision table, and every step had to leave an audit row that the regulator can trace tomorrow. That is an orchestration.

Part V is the story of how the sequence happens. The interesting architectural turn — and the part where APEX-M's design has shifted significantly in the last year — is who does which piece. The outer orchestration (event fired · who do I call · where does the answer go · how does it get audited) is a thin layer: n8n on a developer's laptop, Logic Apps Hybrid on the cloud, or a Foundry workflow when teams want a visual editor. The inner orchestration (how do five specialist agents collaborate to produce the answer) used to live in the outer layer too — sprawling n8n graphs with parallel nodes per agent. That pattern is now an anti-pattern. Microsoft Agent Framework, generally available since 2025, absorbs the inner orchestration cleanly through five named patterns (Sequential · Concurrent · Handoff · Group Chat · Magentic) that each match a different shape of multi-agent reasoning.

The eight chapters below build that story. Chapter 14 names the four recurring scenario shapes (triage-and-decide · continuous-optimization · detect-and-attribute · periodic-digest) and the seven primitives every workflow uses. Chapter 14A covers agent-orchestration archetypes — Microsoft's five patterns — at the conceptual level. Chapter 14B goes deep on Microsoft Agent Framework as the canonical SDK. Chapter 14C covers Responsible AI and Azure AI Content Safety, the runtime guardrails every Service runs. Chapters 15 and 16 describe the now-narrowed substrate role for n8n and Logic Apps Hybrid. Chapter 17 closes with cross-Service composition — how one Service calls another without breaking either's envelope.
