Fabric IQ Adoption Addendum

When the client adopts Microsoft Fabric IQ at the Fabric layer — what changes in the Services Guide.

Currency pin · May 2026

Microsoft has shipped Fabric IQ as a Fabric workload — Ontology · Plan · Graph · Data Agent · Operations Agent · Power BI semantic models. This addendum documents what changes in the Services Guide when a client adopts Fabric IQ instead of the MCP-led path the main volume describes. Existing chapters remain correct for non-Fabric-IQ clients (e.g., Snowflake-on-Azure engagements like Vuori).

Fabric IQ itemStatusKey constraint surfaced by Microsoft Learn
Fabric IQ workloadPREVIEWWhole workload preview-tagged
OntologyPREVIEWManual refresh required for upstream data updates
PlanPREVIEWWriteback against semantic models
GraphPREVIEWRequired tenant setting; backs ontology graph queries via GQL
Data AgentGA5 data sources max · 25-row × 25-column response cap · 100 examples/source · English only · LLM not user-configurable · region-affinity required · history may not persist
Operations AgentPREVIEWTrial capacities not supported · eventhouse OR ontology backing · Teams app required · creator-identity action execution
DLP for Fabric Data WarehouseGADetects and restricts access to sensitive data
Access restriction policies (KQL/SQL/Warehouse)PREVIEWCan block agent access to assets classified sensitive
DSPM Data Risk Assessments · Insider Risk · Agent prompt/response auditPREVIEWPurview governance surface for agents

O.1 The 14 edits, by Services Guide region

Each edit is numbered E1–E14 and cross-references the existing Services Guide chapter it modifies. Edits are additive — read the existing chapter first, then read the edit for the Fabric-IQ-led realization.

Part II · Schemas → Ontology

E1 · Ch 9 (Canonical Schema Layer) reframe. The 14 schema families (SCML · MERML · CXML · PatientML · ClaimML · StudyML · UOGML · P&UML · AXLEML · TELML · MEDML · TECML · TravelerML · ConnectedICEML) ship today as DDL + ERDs. Under Fabric IQ they become Ontology entity-type catalogs — entity types, properties, relationships, condition-action rules (via Activator) — bound to the same Silver tables. The DDL stays for compute economy; the contract surface the agents read becomes the Ontology. Microsoft's canonical example — "Order → Shipment → Temperature Sensor → Cold Chain Breach" — replaces our hand-drawn ERD vignette in the chapter intro.

E2 · New chapter "Ontology Authoring + NL2Ontology". NL2Ontology is a fifth NL2X tool the Data Agent dispatches alongside NL2SQL / NL2DAX / NL2KQL / Microsoft Graph. Per Microsoft Learn: "The ontology layer automatically sends your queries to the most efficient system to get results quickly (such as GQL for Graph in Microsoft Fabric and KQL for Eventhouse)." When a Data Agent's data source is an Ontology, this is the dispatch path. New chapter covers: entity-type design, property typing flow from Silver classification, relationship modeling, binding to lakehouse/eventhouse/semantic-model sources, Activator rule embedding, versioning, governance.

E3 · Refresh semantics surface. The Ontology doc explicitly says: "Any updates in upstream data sources (like new rows) need to be manually refreshed before they're visible in the ontology item." Services Guide §11 (real-time ingestion) needs a new subsection on Ontology refresh cadence.

Part III · MCP catalog bifurcates

E4 · MCP chapter splits Read vs. Action with a precedence lattice. The Data Agent docs make this split explicit and add a governance and intent precedence model (highest to lowest): Organizational → Role-based → Developer → User. This is the canonical authority lattice; the Services Guide MCP catalog chapter and §10 (audit) should adopt the same vocabulary.

E5 · Appendix B (MCP Tool Catalog) reduces with hard constraints. Two Data Agent constraints drive the chunking:

  • 5 data sources max per agent — a single Fabric Data Agent cannot span all 9 sub-domains within a Practice. The Services Guide must specify how Data Agents chunk by sub-domain and how Foundry orchestrates across them.
  • 25-row × 25-column response cap — per Microsoft Learn: "Fabric Data Agents are currently designed for conversational insights rather than for returning complete datasets." Any tool that needs a complete extract must stay as a custom MCP server. The MCP catalog stays roughly half its current size — ~80 of the ~165 tools collapse to Data Agent NL2X reads; ~85 are action or bulk-extract surfaces that remain.

E6 · "Workspace outbound access protection" → PSG-16 candidate. Per Microsoft Learn: "Workspace administrators can manage permitted outbound connections through the workspace settings to control which external endpoints the data agent can reach." Proposed as PSG-16 (Workspace Outbound Boundary), evaluated at deploy time alongside PSG-1..15.

E7 · Foundry as the multi-agent runtime. Direct quote: "External orchestrators and multi-agent runtimes can invoke Fabric data agents to support end-to-end agentic workflows, while the data agents remain focused on read-only, governed data access." The Services Guide's Foundry agent fleet calls Fabric Data Agents via the MicrosoftFabricAgentTool. Service principal authentication is not supported — user-identity (on-behalf-of) passthrough required. Add this constraint to PSG-12 (MCP integrity).

Part IV · Orchestration

E8 · Operations Agent enters as a first-class archetype. Per Microsoft Learn, configuration is goals · instructions · data sources · actions, producing a playbook. Actions wire via Activator + Power Automate flows. The Fabric Operations Agent Teams app is the prescribed notification surface — replaces the custom Adaptive Card webhook pattern for Operations-Agent-led services.

E9 · The creator-identity execution model. Direct quote: "The agent operates by using the delegated identity and permissions of its creator. When a recipient approves a recommendation, the agent executes the action on behalf of the creator, using the creator's permissions." New identity-lattice fact: Operations Agents are creator-bound, not workload-identity-bound the way Foundry agents are. Services Guide §5 (identity) needs a subsection.

E10 · Trial capacities forbidden for Operations Agent. Per Microsoft Learn: "Trial capacities aren't supported." Either upgrade to F2+ or use a Foundry agent stand-in for the laptop substrate.

Part V · Per-Service profiles

E11 · Every Service profile gains an Ontology entity-type list + binding inventory. For each of the 38 Services: which entity types, which relationships, which properties bound to which Silver / Gold tables. The Microsoft Customer · Order · Shipment · Temperature Sensor · Cold Chain Breach shape becomes the per-service template.

E12 · Per-service Data Agent topology. For each Service: how many Data Agents, what each one's 5-source budget covers, which custom MCPs handle write/action. Each profile gets a "Data Agent topology" subsection.

Part VI · Runtime + audit

E13 · §10 (Audit graph) absorbs Purview-side surface. Four Purview-side capabilities (preview) now govern agent traffic: Risk discovery and auditing, DSPM Data Risk Assessments, Insider Risk Management, Audit · eDiscovery · retention. Plus GA DLP for Fabric Data Warehouse and preview access restriction policies for KQL DB / SQL DB / Warehouse.

E14 · ALM section adopts native Fabric mechanics. Per Microsoft Learn, Fabric Data Agents support built-in diagnostics, Git integration (workspace ↔ Git), and Fabric deployment pipelines (dev → test → prod). Services Guide ALM chapter rewrites to layer the APEX deploy.yml workflow on top of Fabric deployment pipelines, with the wizard's PSG gates running before each pipeline-driven promotion.

O.2 Constraints that ripple beyond the 14 edits

ConstraintImplication
English onlyPer-Service capability section must flag English-only as a requirement for Fabric Data Agent path; non-English markets fall back to custom MCP.
Region-affinity requiredData Agent + sources must share workspace capacity region. Affects multi-region tenants.

Conversation history may not persistAudit-row anchoring must come from the source MCP / Activator action, not from Data Agent conversation reconstruction.
Sample queries unsupported for Power BI semantic model sourcesPer-Service authoring guidance differentiates which source type allows example seeding.
Read-perm sufficient for Power BI semantic model access via agentBuild permission no longer needed when access is through Data Agent.

Addendum · Customer Focused Merchandise Pack (CFMP) v0.2

This addendum extends the book with the seventh Industry Solution Pack — Customer Focused Merchandise Pack (CFMP) v0.2 — and documents the six new Virtual Views, three new APEX Core extensions, and Phase-1 live status of the working demo on APEX-M.

Updated Pack catalog (7 packs)

The APEX Pack catalog now includes seven Industry Solution Packs. CFMP is the first organized around a customer-moment spine rather than an operator function — sibling to the operator-side Retail Merchandising Pack v1 (§9.6 of APEX-Architecture-v5).

New Virtual Views shipped with CFMP v0.2

CFMP contributes 6 new Virtual Views spanning MERML (merchandise), CXML (customer experience), and the new cfmp namespace. All are declarative manifests; the runtime federates them through the standard apex-orchestrator data path.

Virtual View IDPurpose
merml.product_with_planogram_locationPer-SKU shelf location joined from MERML.Product × CFMP.StoreMap. Refreshed nightly from the planogram feed; drives the agent's route_to_product tool.
merml.osa_by_aisleOn-shelf availability rolled up by aisle. Combines POS velocity, inventory position, and Vision AI Dev Kit shelf-void detections. Feeds OSA / shelf-gap-restock-dispatch scenarios.
cxml.customer_session_with_routeActive customer phone session enriched with the most recent wayfinding route + current graph node. Backs the customer_phone Adaptive Card transport.
cxml.cart_dwell_eventCart-stationary >5min outside checkout zone event stream. Triggers cart-dwell-abandonment-rescue dispatches via Teams cards to the nearest associate.
cxml.dietary_profileCustomer's active dietary preferences (loyalty-bound; consent-gated). Read by the proactive associate to flag conflicts and propose compliant alternatives.
cfmp.storemap_viewThin overlay binding the retailer store_id to the Azure Maps Creator Dataset ID + Stateset ID + nightly SKU↔unit_id table. Pack-level manifest captured once per store, refreshed on remodel.

Core extensions CFMP introduces

  • New persona type — customer · identity bound to loyalty ID; consent_gate: required; channel customer_phone. Reusable across all future customer-facing Packs (Banking-Customer, Telco-Customer, Hospitality-Guest).
  • New HITL transport — customer_phone · extends interface #9. APEX-M binding: Azure Notification Hubs signed-link push + MCP callback. Same model on G/A.
  • Proposed Interface #15 — Maps & Wayfinding · APEX-M: Azure Maps Creator (Indoor Maps + Wayfinding REST + Web SDK). APEX-G: Google Maps Geospatial Creator. APEX-A: Amazon Location Service indoor maps. Industry Packs consume the abstract interface; the cloud-profile YAML resolves the implementation.
